prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Render a high-fidelity, production-quality desktop WEBSITE HOMEPAGE itself, edge-to-edge, landscape 1536 x 1024. Not a browser window, not a desk, no device mockup. This is a public chapter survey for the one book "Afterlife for an Atheist". The visitor's job is choosing a chapter, not buying a book. Visual world already chosen: quiet literary, refined readable book serif for the title and chapter names, clean humanist sans for controls and body copy. Flat warm off-white background #F5F3ED, deep charcoal text #292B27, muted moss #596448 accents, pale stone rules #DCDCD3. Precise spacing, generous margins, strong readable hierarchy; body copy about 20 px at this image resolution. No decorative border around the page, no glossy cards, no rounded card grid, no drop shadows, no gradients, no grain overlay, no badges, no quotes, no slogans, no catchphrases, no invented author or chapter titles, no religious imagery, no purchase buttons, no newsletter, no fake results or user counts. Illustration is an original ABSTRACT INK STUDY: a few overlapping translucent moss/gray organic oval washes crossed by a few delicately drawn graphite curves, airy and materially hand-made, no lettering or symbols; placed inside the designated illustration region, never behind body copy. It is artwork about perspectives, NOT an afterlife depiction. Include a discrete top bar: small text "Reader survey" left, familiar theme dropdown "Theme: System" right. Exact title "Afterlife for an Atheist". Exact body text "Choose a chapter to rate how convincing you found its case for an afterlife and read or leave comments." Exact chapter section heading "Chapters", supporting instruction "Select the chapter you have read." Nine distinct clickable links labeled "Chapter 1", "Chapter 2", "Chapter 3", "Chapter 4", "Chapter 5", "Chapter 6", "Chapter 7", "Chapter 8", "Chapter 9", each with a small right arrow. Footer links "Privacy" and "Commenting guidelines". Design the complete homepage with all nine links and footer visible. No large primary CTA needed: chapter links are the primary action. Fine visual craft without ornament.
COMPOSITION C — HORIZONTAL REGISTER. Build a compact horizontal title band across the upper third: substantial book title LEFT in a 450px column, a contained shallow ink study in the MIDDLE 300px column, and the factual explanatory copy RIGHT in a 300px column, all with ample separation. Below a quiet dividing rule, the main navigation is THREE OPEN VERTICAL COLUMNS side by side. Left column has Chapter 1, Chapter 2, Chapter 3; middle column has Chapter 4, Chapter 5, Chapter 6; right column has Chapter 7, Chapter 8, Chapter 9. Each chapter link is a roomy typographic row with a small chapter number above or beside the name, arrow aligned right, and fine rule underneath. Not cards: a flat open directory. The nine chapters occupy most of the vertical space, with stronger index density than composition A and no single long list as in B. Place the word Chapters and the supporting instruction directly above this directory. Entire main content area is roughly 1180px wide. This composition should feel precise and browsable with compact title treatment and generous chapter navigation.
